title: Physics — arXiv announcement batch, Thursday 8 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This is a curated editorial selection from the latest announcement batch, not a popularity ranking; citation and independent attention evidence are sparse, and the selected records had zero citation and influential-citation counts in Semantic Scholar at capture.

sections.title: Observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz transition J/ψ→e+e−ηc
sections.abstract: BESIII reports the first observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay J/ψ→e+e−ηc, measuring its rate relative to J/ψ→γηc and extracting the q²-dependent form factors.
sections.claimed_result: The BESIII authors measure the relative branching fraction as (0.65±0.02stat±0.07sys)%; they find no significant deviation of the extracted form factor from theoretical prediction.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; BESIII detector at the BEPCII e+e− collider.
sections.unique_caveat: The result establishes the decay but not a discrepancy with theory; the reported systematic uncertainty is larger than the statistical one.

sections.title: Remote magnon sensing detects the universal phase stiffness jump in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ
sections.abstract: The authors use propagating magnons in CrSBr as remote optical probes of an underdoped cuprate and report a field-induced Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless phase-stiffness jump.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say the magnon group velocity encodes the cuprate's phase stiffness through Meissner screening and reveals a parallel-field-induced BKT transition.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; optical excitation/detection of CrSBr magnon wavepackets in a CrSBr/underdoped-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ heterostructure.
sections.unique_caveat: The inference depends on the magnon-velocity/stiffness calibration and Meissner-screening model in this specific heterostructure; the abstract does not quantify the extraction uncertainty.

sections.title: Extreme Stellar Death and Galaxy Feedback at z=2: A Rest-frame Ultraviolet Characterization of the Strongly Lensed Superluminous Supernova 2025wny
sections.abstract: Keck-II ultraviolet spectroscopy and Pan-STARRS photometry characterize a strongly lensed, hydrogen-poor superluminous supernova at redshift 2.0155, measuring its magnification and host-galaxy properties.
sections.claimed_result: The authors estimate a brightest-image magnification of 19.4±1.6, an outflow speed near 575 km/s, and Lyα escape fraction 0.23±0.03; a magnetar-plus-56Ni fit matches near-peak light but not the late plateau.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; Keck-II/KCWI integral-field spectroscopy and Pan-STARRS photometry, interpreted with a transient light-curve model.
sections.unique_caveat: The late-time plateau points to an additional power source, and the magnetar parameters are model-fit inferences rather than direct measurements of the engine.

sections.title: Toward a complete understanding of the properties of GW190521
sections.abstract: A multi-family waveform reanalysis of the short, massive gravitational-wave event GW190521 finds a highly eccentric interpretation and shows how eccentricity can be confused with spin precession.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer eccentricity 0.81+0.05/-0.01 at 5 Hz and a probability of at least 97% that the primary black hole is in the pair-instability mass gap; secondary mass-gap membership depends on the waveform model.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; gravitational-wave event reanalysis with waveform families, injections, and highly eccentric numerical-relativity waveforms.
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred eccentricity lies beyond the calibration regime of current models; mass and spin conclusions remain waveform/model dependent.

sections.title: Wavelength-Resolved Timing of Near-Infrared Scintillation in Gaseous Xenon
sections.abstract: The authors measure alpha-induced near-infrared xenon scintillation across 12 wavelength bands and separate a fast line-associated component from a slower continuum component.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify a nanosecond-scale fast component and a dominant microsecond-scale component; they infer an approximately 3 μs intrinsic lifetime under a radiative-decay interpretation and find an ionic-dimer transition more consistent with the continuum data.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; alpha-particle interactions in gaseous xenon, measured over approximately 950–1620 nm.
sections.unique_caveat: The emitting-state assignments remain candidate explanations, and the lifetime estimate depends on interpreting the slower kinetic process as radiative decay.

sections.title: Event-by-event net-charge fluctuations in pp, OO, Ne-Ne, and Pb-Pb collisions with ALICE at the LHC
sections.abstract: ALICE studies event-by-event net-electric-charge fluctuations across proton-proton and three nuclear collision systems, comparing their density dependence with several event generators.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a smooth, energy-independent decrease in the magnitude of νdyn[+,-] with increasing system size and a dominance of opposite-sign over like-sign charge correlations.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ALICE data at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, compared with event-generator calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a six-page, one-figure conference proceeding; the fluctuation pattern and generator comparisons alone do not uniquely identify a QGP phase-transition signal.
